He was one of them who fought because he had nothing better to do; if he returned home, he would be sent to prison and never see the light of day ever again. This fact was commonplace in the insurgency forces of the "Salvation Government"; luckily, they did have some military staff. Still, it wasn't enough to provide any meaningful resistance, so what they did instead was horrible things to win against this leviathan. Razing, pillaging, and hit-and-run attacks were frequent in the northern regions along the border between the current government and rebel forces.[/i]

[i]Both sides are locked in what seems to be a self-made state of stalemate. [/i]

[i]After a while, he'd set his book down and leave his tent, seeing his comrades in arms being still alive and one piece filled him with indifference, because he was standing amidst possibly the worst people on this planet. "You're finally awake." The officer sneered as he folded his map and put it away. "I never could sleep with the winter roaring like this." He'd reply to the officer with a grumble; all he could think of now was coffee, but that hadn't been a thing for five years. "I'll go for a walk and watch the perimeter." He continued with a frown. The officer replied with a simple nod, and as such, he went to the makeshift armoury, grabbed a rifle, some magazines, and wandered off with the hopes that there was nothing out there.[/i]

[i]With him on patrol, he could avoid the dirty work which was soon to commence, raids on northern tribal land to claim it and hopefully find new "recruits" and resources. He never approved of it as it was in his eyes, "cruel and unjust". Whenever he could, we would go on patrols, stand guard, and reluctantly take the rear and defend the push. He knew what he was doing, but it was either this or rot in jail for some "silly" crime.[/i]
